title: Compatible stagewise Kan comparison cocone is colimiting
statement:
Let $J$ be a small filtered category, $F:J	o\mathrm{Cat}$ a diagram of small categories, and $V$ a cocone whose object and arrow cocones are colimits of sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit, def-weil-pbc-arrows-functor]. Fix $i\in J$. For $t\in\mathrm{Under}(i)$, let $A_t:F(t.\mathrm{right})^{\mathrm{op}}	o\mathrm{Sets}$ be a presheaf. For $c:t	o t'$ let $	heta_c:A_t	o F(c.\mathrm{right})^{\mathrm{op}}\star A_{t'}$ be a natural transformation, where $\star$ denotes precomposition. Assume identity and composition hold componentwise as objects of $\mathrm{Arrow}(\mathrm{Sets})$, including the endpoint transports from $F$. Let $B:\mathrm{Under}(i)	o\mathrm{PSh}(V.\mathrm{pt})$ and $ eta_t:A_t	o V_t^{\mathrm{op}}\star B_t$ exhibit $B_t$ as a left Kan extension along $V_t^{\mathrm{op}}$, with $V_t=V_{t.\mathrm{right}}$. A left Kan extension here means that composing with $ eta_t$ bijects natural transformations $B_t	o T$ with natural transformations $A_t	o V_t^{\mathrm{op}}\star T$ for every presheaf $T$ on $V.\mathrm{pt}$. Assume $ eta_t$ followed by $B(c)$ equals $	heta_c$ followed by $ eta_{t'}$ componentwise in $\mathrm{Arrow}(\mathrm{Sets})$. Fix $j,k\in J$ and $a:i	o k$, $b:j	o k$. Let $s=\mathrm{Under.map}(a):\mathrm{Under}(k)	o\mathrm{Under}(i)$ send $(k\xrightarrow{t.\mathrm{hom}}l)$ to $(i\xrightarrow{a\,;\,t.\mathrm{hom}}l)$, and write $g_t=F(b\,;\,t.\mathrm{hom})$, where a semicolon means composition in diagram order. Let $D:\mathrm{Under}(k)	o\mathrm{PSh}(F(j))$ be a diagram with isomorphisms $e_t:D_t\cong g_t^{\mathrm{op}}\star A_{s(t)}$. Assume $D(c)_U\,;\,e_{t',U}=e_{t,U}\,;\,	heta_{s(c),g_t^{\mathrm{op}}(U)}$ in $\mathrm{Arrow}(\mathrm{Sets})$ for every $c:t	o t'$ and $U\in F(j)^{\mathrm{op}}$. Let $
u$ be a cocone on $D$ with vertex $V_j^{\mathrm{op}}\star\operatorname{colim}B$. Assume $
u_{t,U}$ is, in $\mathrm{Arrow}(\mathrm{Sets})$, the composite of $e_{t,U}$, the component of $ eta_{s(t)}$ at $g_t^{\mathrm{op}}(U)$, and the outer coprojection for $B$ at $V_{t.\mathrm{right}}^{\mathrm{op}}(g_t^{\mathrm{op}}(U))$. Then $
u$ is colimiting, formally $\mathrm{Nonempty}(\mathrm{IsColimit}(
u))$. This assertion constructs no sheaf diagram and uses no topology.

proof.text: For each object U of F(j), use the pointwise left Kan presentation of every B(t) and Types.jointly_surjective for the outer colimit. A generator is a section x of A(t) at X together with an arrow V(j)(U) to V(t.right)(X). Represent this arrow using harrows. Refine using hobjects to identify its endpoints with the chosen representatives of U and X. Choose a common stage receiving k and t.right, and equalize the maps out of i, obtaining tprime in Under k and a morphism t to Under.map(a)(tprime). Apply theta to x and restrict along the lifted arrow. The inverse of e(tprime) gives a D generator. Naturality of beta and hbeta_map, followed by hnu, show that it maps to the original outer Kan generator. This proves surjectivity of the map induced by nu.

proof.text: For injectivity, represent the two D elements at stages of Under k. Equality of their images in the outer filtered colimit B is eventual equality at one stage of Under i. Pointwise Kan equality there is generated by a finite chain of section restrictions. Lift all arrows and all endpoint equations of this chain to a common stage via hobjects and harrows. Equalize the finitely many maps from k and make all image-arrow equations hold by the filtered-set equality criterion. At this common stage, naturality of beta accounts for each Kan restriction relation and hbeta_map accounts for each outer transition relation. The formula hD identifies the resulting transitions with those of D. Consequently the two elements have the same image at a later D stage and hence define the same colimit D element. The identity and composition assumptions on theta permit flattening all stage refinements in this finite chain.

proof.text: The morphism colimit D to nu.pt induced by nu is natural in U and has bijective components by the previous steps. Thus it is a presheaf isomorphism. Transport the colimit universal property across this isomorphism to obtain IsColimit nu, and take its Nonempty wrapper. No topology or sheaf inverse-image construction is used.

theorem colimit_stage_kan_cocone
    (J : Type u) [SmallCategory J] [IsFiltered J] (F : J ⥤ Cat.{u, u})
    (V : Cocone F)
    (hobjects : IsColimit (Cat.objects.mapCocone V))
    (harrows : IsColimit (Cat.arrows.mapCocone V))
    (i : J) (A : ∀ t : Under i, (F.obj t.right)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (θ : ∀ (t t' : Under i) (c : t ⟶ t'),
      A t ⟶ (F.map c.right).toFunctor.op ⋙ A t')
    (hθid : ∀ (t : Under i) (X : (F.obj t.right)ᵒᵖ),
      Arrow.mk ((θ t t (𝟙 t)).app X) = Arrow.mk (𝟙 ((A t).obj X)))
    (hθcomp : ∀ (t t' t'' : Under i) (c : t ⟶ t') (d : t' ⟶ t'')
        (X : (F.obj t.right)ᵒᵖ),
      Arrow.mk ((θ t t' c).app X ≫
        (θ t' t'' d).app ((F.map c.right).toFunctor.op.obj X)) =
      Arrow.mk ((θ t t'' (c ≫ d)).app X))
    (B : Under i ⥤ (V.ptᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u))
    (β : ∀ t : Under i, A t ⟶ (V.ι.app t.right).toFunctor.op ⋙ B.obj t)
    (hβ : ∀ t : Under i, (B.obj t).IsLeftKanExtension (β t))
    (hβmap : ∀ (t t' : Under i) (c : t ⟶ t') (X : F.obj t.right),
      Arrow.mk ((β t).app (op X) ≫
        (B.map c).app (op ((V.ι.app t.right).toFunctor.obj X))) =
      Arrow.mk ((θ t t' c).app (op X) ≫
        (β t').app (op ((F.map c.right).toFunctor.obj X))))
    (j k : J) (a : i ⟶ k) (b : j ⟶ k)
    (D : Under k ⥤ ((F.obj j)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u))
    (e : ∀ t : Under k, D.obj t ≅
      (F.map (b ≫ t.hom)).toFunctor.op ⋙ A ((Under.map a).obj t))
    (hD : ∀ (t t' : Under k) (c : t ⟶ t') (U : (F.obj j)ᵒᵖ),
      Arrow.mk ((D.map c).app U ≫ (e t').hom.app U) =
      Arrow.mk ((e t).hom.app U ≫
        (θ ((Under.map a).obj t) ((Under.map a).obj t') ((Under.map a).map c)).app
          ((F.map (b ≫ t.hom)).toFunctor.op.obj U)))
    (ν : Cocone D)
    (hpt : ν.pt = (V.ι.app j).toFunctor.op ⋙ colimit B)
    (hν : ∀ (t : Under k) (U : (F.obj j)ᵒᵖ),
      Arrow.mk ((ν.ι.app t).app U) =
      Arrow.mk ((e t).hom.app U ≫
        (β ((Under.map a).obj t)).app ((F.map (b ≫ t.hom)).toFunctor.op.obj U) ≫
        (colimit.ι B ((Under.map a).obj t)).app
          ((V.ι.app t.right).toFunctor.op.obj
            ((F.map (b ≫ t.hom)).toFunctor.op.obj U)))) :
    Nonempty (IsColimit ν)
